restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5: lanes are held one per register; one six-round PERM6 call costs 1 unit and reads its 25 operand registers without writing them (the reference data path of exactly C = 1626 operations, traced in proof Appendix B), and every other primitive costs 1/1626 units, with jumps, moves, immediate register writes and the call issue each charged as one operation.

Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x) = LE32(x); the 21 constant padding and capacity lanes are written once at setup and never modified.

Generic van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search run on one processor: a point is distinguished when its output lane 0 is below 2^32 (theta = 2^-32), maximum chain length 2^40, evaluation budget K0 = 8340625*2^105, record cap 2^98, main loop unrolled 256 times with a DP test (compare, branch) after every evaluation, one run with no restart.

Time, memory and preprocessing are worst-case bounds for every run (log2 T <= 127.99439380). The success probability of at least 0.39 (exactly bounded below by 0.3900000103 under H-RF) holds under the declared random-function heuristic H-RF.

Generic attack with no cryptanalytic improvement claimed; no stored collision, advice or precomputation. Same algorithm family and heuristic as our earlier accepted package for this track (submission 1e370c6c, 128.014); only the accounting is tightened (proof Section 0).

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x) = SHA3-256-r6(LE32(x)) on 256-bit words x: whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point it has not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of every value observed so far. This is the standard premise of the van Oorschot-Wiener analysis. It is used only to lower-bound the success probability (Section 6). Output correctness (Section 5) and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds (Sections 4, 7 and 8) are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: The fixed six-round prefix SHA3-256 restricted to 32-byte messages, iterated along pseudo-random chains from uniformly random 256-bit starts. The analysis uses only the chains started before the first contact (expected number at most 1 + K0*2^-32 + K0*2^-40 < 2^96; at most 2^98 + 2^88 + 1 chains in any run) and at most K0 - 1 + 2^40 < 2^128 main-loop evaluations, with K0 = 8340625*2^105.
heuristics.extrapolation: We ran the distinguished-point search of Section 4 (in the variant of our earlier package, see proof Section 9; the step map f is identical) (with n-bit starts, a hash map in place of the trie and no record cap) on output-truncated versions of the real six-round map (n = 24, 32, 40 and 48 bits) and compared it with a keyed 24-round control. These tests are extrapolated to the full 256-bit map. The analytic success bound itself uses only the H-RF statement, not the measured numbers.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is false as a literal statement about a fixed deterministic function; it is a heuristic model. The supporting experiments are our own and are not organizer-executed (no experiment manifest is declared); their full source and exact arguments are in the proof so every row can be regenerated. They cover only output widths of 24-48 bits on n-bit input subsets and cannot exclude a structural property that appears only at full width. The success bound exceeds 0.39 by only 1.0e-8; if H-RF overstated the contact probability by a small delta, restoring 0.39 would add about 2.4*delta bits to the scalar.
